title: Prevent page slug normalization from overwriting content
description:
Problem: human-friendly page normalization is many-to-one. Distinct titles or imported slugs can converge on the same storage path, and a later write can silently replace existing content without a conflict or revision precondition.

Desired outcome: page creation and update semantics preserve content integrity and make normalization collisions explicit.

Scope:
- Separate create from update behavior.
- Require an existing revision or equivalent precondition for updates.
- Detect normalization collisions and return a conflict, deterministic alternate slug, or reviewable proposal.
- Add migration or diagnostics coverage for existing ambiguous paths.
- Out of scope: changing safe traversal validation for task-linked page references.

Acceptance criteria:
- Two distinct inputs that normalize to the same slug cannot silently lose the first page.
- Updates require an explicit target and revision/ETag policy.
- Conflict responses identify the safe next action without leaking unrelated page content.
- Agent and bulk-import writes use the same collision policy.
- Tests cover create, update, retry, collision, and concurrent-write scenarios.

Validation:
- Run focused page-storage and API contract tests.
- Run page-link and task-record validation where affected.
- Run Test-TaskRecords.ps1 after task metadata changes.
